answer: Epoch-Linked Reputation Carryover. Each identity's reputation converts to a vine that only survives if the identity keeps issuing the same signed behaviour attestations across epochs, so a fresh alias starts from zero and must re-earn standing. The nectar held by that vine is frozen whenever a discontinuity appears, forcing the operator to either sustain honest activity or forfeit accumulated value. An attacker therefore pays a jetty of repeated honest epochs per alias before it can affect anything, multiplying the real cost across every identity they create.
